groups.sentence: Administrators give AI agents unique non-human identities and enforce least-privilege access to systems, data and tools.
Users must not share passwords, credentials, API keys, tokens or other secrets with AI tools or agents.
Code generated by AI is reviewed and approved before use in production or institutional IT systems.
Users enable extra security such as VPN or additional authentication when accessing AI tools.
Users restrict permissions granted to AI applications to only what is necessary.
Users sandbox and clearly scope AI agents and bots used for university purposes.
Users secure AI systems and university resources, and consult the security office.
Users use university-authenticated or managed accounts and compliant devices, not personal accounts, for AI tools.
Users must not connect AI tools or agents to university systems or data without approval.
Administrators limit information access to authorized personnel and protect AI systems against cyber threats.
AI-generated code may contain bugs, security vulnerabilities or logic errors.
Administrators require multi-factor authentication and encryption for AI access and environments.
